SELECT * FROM users
sql.why: WHERE filters rows before grouping.

sql.code:
-- Which clause filters grouped results?
SELECT team, COUNT(*) FROM players GROUP BY team
sql.why: HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

sql.code: -- Which keyword removes duplicate result rows?
sql.why: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the result.

sql.code: -- Which join returns only matching rows?
sql.why: INNER JOIN returns rows matching the join condition.

sql.code: -- Which function counts rows?
sql.why: COUNT(*) counts rows.

sql.code: -- Which clause sorts results?
sql.why: ORDER BY sorts the result set.

sql.code: -- How do you test for missing values?
sql.why: NULL is tested with IS NULL.

sql.code: -- Which statement changes existing rows?
sql.why: UPDATE modifies existing rows.

sql.code: -- Which command removes rows matching a condition?
sql.why: DELETE removes selected rows.

sql.code: -- Which aggregate calculates an average?
sql.why: AVG calculates the average.

sql.code: -- Which clause groups rows for aggregation?
sql.why: GROUP BY forms groups of rows.

sql.code: -- What does LEFT JOIN preserve?
options: All rows from the left table
sql.why: LEFT JOIN keeps every left-table row.

sql.code: -- Which statement creates a table?
sql.why: CREATE TABLE defines a table.

sql.code: -- Which command adds new rows?
sql.why: INSERT INTO adds rows.

sql.code: -- What does COUNT(column) typically ignore?
sql.why: COUNT(column) ignores NULL values.

sql.code: -- Which operator matches a text pattern?
sql.why: LIKE supports patterns using wildcards such as % and _.

sql.code: -- Which is a common wildcard for any sequence in LIKE?
sql.why: % matches zero or more characters in LIKE patterns.

sql.code: -- What does a primary key enforce?
sql.why: A primary key uniquely identifies each row and cannot be NULL.

sql.code: -- Which clause limits returned rows in common SQL dialects?
sql.why: LIMIT is supported by many SQL dialects.

sql.code: -- Which function returns the largest value?
sql.why: MAX returns the maximum value.

java.why: class declares a Java class.

java.why: boolean is Java’s Boolean primitive type.

java.code: // Which keyword creates an object?
java.why: new creates an object and invokes its constructor.

java.code: // Which collection is an ordered resizable list?
java.why: ArrayList maintains order and supports indexed access.

java.code: // Which keyword prevents reassignment of a variable?
java.why: final prevents reassignment after initialization.

java.code: // Which construct handles exceptions?
java.why: try/catch handles exceptions.

java.why: extends declares class inheritance.

java.code: // Which keyword indicates an interface is implemented?

java.code: // Which access modifier restricts access to the declaring class?
java.why: private restricts access to the declaring class context.

java.code: // Which loop tests its condition before each iteration?
java.why: while checks its condition before each iteration.

java.code: // Which floating-point type has more precision than float?
java.why: double is Java’s 64-bit binary floating-point type.

java.code: // Which keyword exits a method and may return a value?
java.why: return exits a method and can provide its result.

java.code: // Which keyword refers to superclass members or constructors?

java.code: // What happens when you call a method on a null reference?

Several methods with the same name but different parameter lists
A method with too many lines

java.code: // What is method overriding?
options: A subclass providing its own version of a parent method with the same signature

options: Asks the compiler to check that the method really overrides one in a supertype

java.code: // What is an abstract class?
options: A class that only has static methods

java.code: // How many classes can a Java class extend?
java.why: Java has single inheritance of classes but a class can implement many interfaces.

java.why: RuntimeExceptions are unchecked.

java.code: // What does hashCode need to be consistent with?

java.code: // What is a record in Java?

kotlin.why: Composables can call other composables.

kotlin.code: // What does remember { mutableStateOf(0) } do in Compose?
options: Keeps state across recompositions; changes trigger recomposition
kotlin.why: rememberSaveable survives configuration changes.

kotlin.code: // Which keyword marks a class whose members can be overridden?
kotlin.why: Methods also need open to be overridable.

kotlin.code: // What does override do?
options: Marks a member that replaces one from a supertype
kotlin.why: It is required, not optional, in Kotlin.

kotlin.code: // What does an interface in Kotlin allow that a Java 7 interface did not?
kotlin.why: Kotlin interfaces can contain implemented methods.

kotlin.code: // What is the difference between List and MutableList?
options: List is read-only; MutableList adds add, remove and set
kotlin.why: Read-only does not mean immutable underneath.

kotlin.code: // What does the === operator check?
options: Whether two references point to the same object
kotlin.why: == calls equals.

kotlin.code: // What is the Kotlin equivalent of Java's void?
kotlin.why: Nothing is the type of expressions that never return, like throw.

kotlin.code: // How do you throw an exception?
kotlin.why: There is no new keyword in Kotlin.

kotlin.code: // What does require(x > 0) do?
options: Throws IllegalArgumentException if the condition is false
kotlin.why: check throws IllegalStateException instead.

kotlin.code: // Which annotation marks a JUnit test in Kotlin?
kotlin.why: Kotlin uses JUnit and other JVM test frameworks.

kotlin.code: // What file holds Gradle build settings written in Kotlin?
kotlin.why: The .kts extension means Kotlin script.

bash.code: # Which character begins variable expansion?
bash.why: Use $name or ${name} to expand a shell variable.

bash.code: # Which command prints text?
bash.why: echo writes arguments to standard output.

bash.code: # Which command changes the working directory?
# Which command lists directory entries?
# Which command prints the working directory?
bash.why: pwd prints the current working directory.

bash.code: # Which token pipes one command’s output to another?
bash.why: A pipe sends standard output to another command’s standard input.

bash.code: # Which operator redirects output and overwrites a file?
bash.why: > redirects output and normally truncates the destination.

bash.code: # Which operator appends output to a file?
# Which keyword starts a conditional?
bash.why: if starts a conditional command list.

bash.code: # Which keyword closes a Bash if block?
# Which keyword closes for and while loops?
bash.why: done closes for, while, and until loops.

bash.code: # Which syntax performs command substitution?
bash.why: $(...) runs a command and substitutes its output.

bash.code: # Which test checks whether a path exists?
bash.why: The -e test succeeds when a path exists.

bash.code: # Which variable contains the previous command’s exit status?
bash.why: $? expands to the previous command’s exit status.

bash.code: # Which shebang selects Bash through env?
bash.why: The env shebang locates Bash through PATH.

bash.code: # Which command shows the current directory?
# How do you read a variable named NAME?
# Which assignment is correct?
bash.why: There must be no spaces around = in an assignment.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
X=5
echo "$X apples"

# What does this print?
X=5
echo '$X apples'
# Which exit status means success?
# What does | do?
options: Sends one command's output to another command's input
bash.why: ls | wc -l counts lines of ls output.

bash.code: # What does > file do?
options: Writes output to file, replacing its contents

bash.code: # Which command makes script.sh executable?
bash.why: The execute permission lets you run ./script.sh.

bash.code: # What should the first line of a Bash script usually be?
bash.why: The shebang tells the system which interpreter to use.

bash.code: # What does $1 contain inside a script?
options: The first argument passed to the script
bash.why: $0 is the script name, $# the count.

bash.code: # Which test checks whether a file exists?
bash.why: -f tests for a regular file; -d for a directory.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo -n "$i"
done
# What does && do between two commands?
options: Runs the second only if the first failed
Runs the second only if the first succeeded
bash.why: || runs the second only on failure.

bash.code: # Which command searches file contents for text?
bash.why: find searches names; grep searches contents.

bash.code: # What does $(command) do?
options: Runs the command in the background
Replaces itself with the command's output

bash.code: # Why should variables usually be quoted, as in "$FILE"?
options: So values with spaces are not split into several words

bash.code: # Which option stops a script at the first failing command?
bash.why: set -euo pipefail is a common safe header.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
echo $((7 + 3 * 2))
# Which command shows the last lines of a log file as it grows?
bash.why: -f follows new lines as they are written.

bash.code: # What does 2> errors.txt redirect?
# What does $? hold?
options: The exit status of the last command
bash.why: Check it right after the command.

bash.code: # Which loop reads a file line by line safely?
options: while IFS= read -r line; do ...; done < file
bash.why: for over $(cat) splits on spaces too.

bash.code: # Which command changes to your home directory?
# What does chmod 600 secret.txt allow?
options: Read and write for the owner only
bash.why: 6 = read + write for the owner; 0 for group and others.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
echo $((10 / 3))

# What does this print?
echo $((10 % 3))

# What does this print?
echo $((2 ** 5))

# What does this print?
x=4
((x++))
echo $x

# What does this print?
name="Ada"
echo "Hi, ${name}!"

bash.why: ## removes the longest matching prefix up to the last dot.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
echo ${unset_var:-default}
bash.why: :- substitutes a default when unset or empty.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
s="a b c"
for w in $s; do echo -n "[$w]"; done

# What does this print?
s="a b c"
for w in "$s"; do echo -n "[$w]"; done
bash.why: Quoting keeps the value as one word.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
arr=(a b)
arr+=(c)
echo "${arr[@]}"

# What does this print?
declare -A age
age[ada]=36
echo ${age[ada]}

# What does this print?
for i in {1..3}; do echo -n $i; done

# What does this print?
for ((i=0; i<3; i++)); do echo -n $i; done

# What does this print?
i=0
while [ $i -lt 3 ]; do i=$((i+1)); done
echo $i
bash.why: The loop stops when i is no longer less than 3.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
if [ 5 -gt 3 ]; then echo yes; else echo no; fi

# What does this print?
if [ "abc" = "abc" ]; then echo same; fi

# What does this print?
if [[ "file.txt" == *.txt ]]; then echo text; fi
bash.why: [[ ]] supports glob pattern matching on the right.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
x=""
if [ -z "$x" ]; then echo empty; fi

bash.why: $1 inside a function is its first argument.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
f() { return 3; }
f
echo $?
bash.why: return sets the function's exit status.
Command substitution captures the function's output.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
f() { local x=1; }
x=5
f
echo $x
bash.why: local keeps x inside the function.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
true && echo A || echo B
bash.why: true succeeds, so the && branch runs.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
false && echo A || echo B
bash.why: false fails, so the || branch runs.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
echo "a b c" | wc -w

# What does this print?
printf "%s-%s\n" x y
bash.why: printf substitutes arguments into the format.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
printf "%03d\n" 7

# What does this print?
echo "b a c" | tr ' ' '\n' | sort | head -n 1
bash.why: tr splits into lines; sort orders them; head takes the first.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
printf "a
b
a
" | sort | uniq | wc -l
bash.why: uniq removes adjacent duplicates after sorting.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
echo "one,two,three" | cut -d, -f2
bash.why: cut splits on the delimiter and picks field 2.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
echo "hello world" | awk '{print $2}'

# What does this print?
echo "cat" | sed 's/c/b/'
bash.why: sed s replaces the first match on each line.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
echo "aaa" | sed 's/a/b/g'
bash.why: The g flag replaces every match.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
echo "x" > f.txt
echo "y" >> f.txt
wc -l < f.txt
bash.why: > creates the file and >> appends a second line.

bash.code:
# What does this print?
ls /does-not-exist 2>/dev/null
echo $?
options: A non-zero status (2 on GNU ls)
bash.why: The error message is discarded but the command still fails.

bash.code: # What does 2>&1 mean?
options: Send standard error to the same place as standard output

bash.code: # What does /dev/null do?
# What does command & do?
options: Runs it only if the last one succeeded
Runs the command in the background

bash.code: # What does wait do in a script?
options: Waits for background jobs to finish

bash.code: # What does export VAR=value do?
options: Makes the variable available to child processes
bash.why: Put it in ~/.bashrc to make it persistent.

bash.code: # What does source file.sh (or . file.sh) do?
options: Runs it in a new shell
Runs the file in the current shell, so its variables stay set

bash.code: # What does $# contain?
# Why use "$@" rather than $* when passing arguments on?
options: "$@" keeps each argument separate, even with spaces

bash.code: # What does shift do?
options: Drops $1 and moves the other arguments down
bash.why: Useful for parsing options in a loop.

bash.code: # What does set -u do?
options: Treats using an unset variable as an error
bash.why: It catches typos in variable names.

bash.code: # What does set -x do?
options: Prints each command before running it, for debugging

bash.code: # What does set -o pipefail change?
options: A pipeline fails if any command in it fails, not just the last
bash.why: Without it, a failing first command is hidden.

bash.code: # What does trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT do?
options: Runs the clean-up command when the script exits

bash.code: # What does mktemp create?
options: A new temporary file with a unique name

bash.code: # What does find . -name "*.log" do?
options: Lists files below the current folder whose names end in .log

bash.code: # What does xargs do in find . -name "*.tmp" | xargs rm?
options: Turns input lines into arguments for rm
bash.why: Use find -print0 | xargs -0 for names with spaces.

bash.code: # What does chmod u+x run.sh do?
options: Adds execute permission for the file's owner
bash.why: u is user, g group, o others.

bash.code: # What does chmod 755 give?
options: Owner read/write/execute; group and others read/execute

bash.code: # What does sudo do?
options: Runs a command as another user, usually root

bash.code: # What does ps aux show?
# What does kill -9 PID do?
options: Forcibly ends the process without letting it clean up

bash.code: # What does df -h show?
options: Free and used disk space in human-readable units
bash.why: du -sh shows the size of a folder.

bash.code: # What does curl -s URL do?
options: Downloads the URL and prints it, without the progress meter

bash.code: # What does a here-document (<<EOF ... EOF) provide?
options: Multi-line text as standard input to a command
bash.why: Quote 'EOF' to stop variable expansion inside.

bash.code: # What does read -p "Name: " name do?
options: Prompts and stores the typed line in $name

bash.code: # What does the shebang #!/usr/bin/env bash do differently from #!/bin/bash?
options: Finds bash on the PATH instead of using a fixed location
bash.why: It helps on systems where bash lives elsewhere.

bash.code: # Which tool checks shell scripts for common bugs?
bash.why: It warns about unquoted variables and more.

bash.code: # What is the exit status of a pipeline by default?
options: The status of the last command
The status of the first command

bash.code: # What does [ -d "$dir" ] test?
# What does [ -n "$x" ] test?
# What does ~/.bashrc contain?
options: Commands run when an interactive Bash shell starts
bash.why: Aliases and PATH changes go here.

bash.code: # What does alias ll='ls -la' do?
bash.why: Put it in ~/.bashrc to keep it.
